column1: # Game profile of Celeste (Switch, update 1.4.1.1 = v589824, the game shows v.1.4.1.0; base game v0 not extracted). Plays on the Mac (title, file select, the prologue at 60 fps with sound) and on the iPhone
# MonoGame for the Switch (Microsoft.Xna.Framework over NVN), its C# and the game's compiled to C++ by Sickhead's BRUTE into main, FMOD Studio sound through AudioOut, SDK 15.3.2.

# The shaders are MonoGame effects (MGFX version 8): 13 in Content/Effects/*.xnb, and SpriteBatch's built-in effect in main (shader_split.py mgfx_effect). The provisional profile's guesses held: no key needed changing

# Game name: only a label for profile listings and the Mac window title; the iOS app name is the game name in the base NSP, and the bundle ID comes from the base game title ID (build_ipa.sh / NSP script)
# only the merged 1.4.1.1 copy is extracted
# The NPDM declares no system resource, so the game has no virtual address memory: it sets a heap of the application pool − used memory (3.11 GB) and allocates from it.
# The block is 256 MB in front + 256 MB alias region + 256 MB stack region + 3.25 GB heap region
# the NPDM declares no system resource: IsVirtualAddressMemoryEnabled is false, as on Horizon
# the rewritten modules are larger than the default 64 MB of used memory (BRUTE's main alone is 78 MB with its bss), so the heap request plus the modules would exceed the pool
